one_line: A South Indian merchant donor and temple accountant managing ritual endowments in medieval market towns and port cities.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, lean but sturdy build, slightly stooped from long hours of writing and travel.
appearance.face: Oval face with medium-brown South Indian complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, expressive dark eyes with a focused, calculating gaze, a small horizontal white forehead mark with a red central streak, default expression calm and observant with a hint of shrewdness.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair oiled and combed back into a neat low knot at the back of the head, with a thin cloth headband in muted red holding it, no turban or crown.
appearance.costume: A knee-length off-white cotton angarkha-style upper garment wrapped right-over-left and tied with inner cords, its borders edged with a narrow dull-gold woven line; beneath, a full-length unbleached cotton veshti/dhoti wrapped securely around the waist and falling to the ankles with a single front pleat, hem edged in dark indigo; over the left shoulder a soft, slightly worn, plain deep-maroon cotton angavastram draped diagonally across the chest and back; simple brown leather sandals on the feet; minimal jewellery of a thin gold chain tucked under the angarkha and a single plain copper bangle on the right wrist; a small palm-leaf manuscript bundle tucked at the waist and a narrow cloth belt subtly cinching the garments for movement.
appearance.signature: A rectangular wooden writing board held under the left arm, with a looped palm-leaf manuscript bundle and a reed stylus tied to it by a thin cotton cord, edges darkened from use.

ref_desc: A mid-30s South Indian man with medium-brown skin, oiled black hair in a low knot with red headband, short beard, off-white angarkha, unbleached dhoti with dark indigo border, deep-maroon angavastram, simple sandals, and a well-used wooden writing board with palm-leaf manuscripts and stylus.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a mid-30s South Indian male temple merchant-accountant standing in a neutral pose: he has an oval medium-brown face, sharp nose, short beard and moustache, expressive dark eyes and a small horizontal white forehead mark with a red streak; his thick black hair is oiled, combed back and tied in a neat low knot at the back of the head, secured with a thin muted-red cloth headband. He wears an off-white knee-length cotton angarkha-style upper garment wrapped right-over-left and edged with a narrow dull-gold woven border, over a full-length unbleached cotton veshti/dhoti wrapped around the waist, falling to the ankles with a single front pleat and a dark indigo hem. A deep-maroon cotton angavastram is draped from his left shoulder diagonally across his chest and back, slightly worn but neatly arranged. On his feet are simple brown leather sandals; jewellery is minimal, just a thin gold chain mostly hidden under the angarkha and a plain copper bangle on his right wrist. A narrow cloth belt subtly gathers his waist, with a small bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts tucked in. His signature prop, a rectangular wooden writing board with a looped bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts and a reed stylus tied by a thin cotton cord, is held securely under his left arm; the board’s edges show darkened wear. Use a colour palette of off-white, deep maroon, dark indigo, dull gold accents and brown leather, and present him from head to toe with clear views of his hairstyle, facial features, layered garments and the wooden writing board with attached palm-leaf manuscripts and stylus.
